Hi Lars —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to learn more about NordBank's roadmap for customer-facing assistants and the regulatory constraints you're juggling across the Nordics and EU. Quick recap and recommended next steps: 

1) Key constraints you shared
- EU-only data residency for customer PII and transaction logs
- Some high-risk workloads (fraud models) may need to run in customer-managed VPC or on-premise in a future phase
- Target latency for customer-facing chat: <= 200ms median

2) Deployment modes that fit your needs (brief)
- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted, EU-region): fastest to get started, supports EU residency when pinned to our EU regions; best for quick POC/demo.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): predictable throughput and stronger isolation; can be provisioned in EU regions and offers private networking options.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed keys, recommended for regulated workloads or when you require no cross-region routing.

3) Action items I can own this week
- Share EU/APAC region availability doc + SOC2 attestation (attached).
- Sketch an initial mutual action plan with milestones for POC (2 weeks), Dedicated sizing (3-4 weeks), and Private evaluation (4-8 weeks).
- Connect you with our Solutions Architect (Aditya) for technical sizing and network requirements.

Are you available for a 30-min technical sync with Aditya on Tuesday 2027-06-29? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read.

Attached: Redwood_EU_APAC_Region_Overview.pdf, SOC2_Type2_Attestation.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan_NordBank.xlsx

Best,
Lauren

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear recap — very helpful. A few clarifying questions before we lock the demo and tech sync: 

- EU-only: When you say "pin to EU regions," does that guarantee that both data-at-rest and all inference traffic stay inside EU clouds (no optional fallbacks to us regions)? We need guarantees for transaction logs and embeddings.
- Cross-region routing: Our compliance team is concerned about any cross-region proxying for burst capacity. If Dedicated capacity in EU is temporarily saturated, would Hosted fallback ever route to non-EU?
- Private option: Curious what the timeline and minimum commitment looks like for a Private VPC deployment — and whether we can start with Private in a single AZ in Frankfurt for a POC.

Also happy to take the SOC2 doc; can you confirm the redacted fields are acceptable to procurement.

Available for Tue 6/29 at 10:00 CET — please send invite.

Cheers,
Lars

Looping in some quick notes ahead of the tech sync: 

- EU residency guarantee: We can guarantee storage and processing inside EU regions when a customer selects EU-hosted or Dedicated EU capacity. Redwood's control plane may be US-based by default for hosted customers, but for enterprise contracts we provide a private control plane option (part of our Private offering) or a dedicated control plane that can be localized. For NordBank's needs, recommend Dedicated in EU for the POC to avoid any control-plane residency questions.
- Fallbacks: We do not automatically route to non-EU regions for reserved Dedicated capacity. Hosted customers using multi-region setups may have fallback policies, but we can configure strict region pinning in the routing policy for enterprise deals.
- Private POC: We can provision a Private VPC with minimal footprint for a POC in a single AZ (Frankfurt) — delivery timeline ~4-6 weeks depending on legal & network approvals.

I can own a short technical pre-read for the Tue sync: proposed agenda (30m) — network requirements (VPC peering, egress), key management (KMS/HSM options), model variants to start with, and latency expectations.

—Aditya

Thanks Lars — sending invite for Tue 29 at 10:00 CET (calendar invite sent). A few quick answers inline to help procurement: 

- "Guarantee" = yes for data-at-rest and inference processing when pinned to EU Dedicated or Private — that includes embeddings and logs. Our standard Hosted tiers can be pinned to EU regions but enterprise language in the contract + technical controls are recommended for iron-clad guarantees.
- Fallbacks = we will configure routing policies so Dedicated EU capacity will not fail over to non-EU regions. For Hosted we can also enforce region-only routing but it requires a routing policy clause in the SOW.
- Private POC = we can start in a single AZ (Frankfurt). Timeline estimate 4-6 weeks; minimal commit for Private starts at a quarterly support + onboarding retainer (I included a line item in the mutual action plan).

I've attached the SOC2 PDF and region overview; Procurement, please review the SOC2 redactions and flag any missing evidence.

See you Tue.

Best,
Lauren
